hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding through 2029
hero.body:
The Senate approved legislation early Friday to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's second term, following an intense overnight session. The final vote was 52-47, with Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska as the only Republican voting against the bill and Senator Michael Bennet of Colorado not voting.

The legislation provides approximately $70 billion in new funding for the Department of Homeland Security's immigration enforcement operations over three years. Senate Republicans secured passage after an 18-hour marathon voting session known as a vote-a-rama, a process where senators propose and vote on amendments to legislation passed through the budget reconciliation procedure.

Democratic leaders attempted to use the extended voting period to force Republicans to defend controversial provisions within the bill. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer had pledged to leverage the vote-a-rama to highlight what he characterized as priorities favoring Trump. According to Schumer, "Senate Republicans passed a rotten bill that makes their priorities painfully clear: more money for Donald Trump, more power for Donald Trump, and nothing to lower costs for working families."

During the voting marathon, Democrats introduced an amendment attempting to eliminate an "anti-weaponization fund" and block Trump from establishing a settlement fund worth $1.8 billion. The amendment narrowly failed with a vote of 49-50, after three Republican senators joined all Democrats in support. Democrats also succeeded in forcing Republicans to withdraw a separate proposal for $1 billion in security improvements for the White House ballroom.

Republican Senator Lindsey Graham expressed satisfaction with the outcome, stating he was "very proud of my Republican colleagues for sticking together and making sure that Border Patrol and ICE are fully funded." He added, "Well done to President Trump and my Republican colleagues."

If signed into law, the bill would remove ICE and Border Patrol funding from annual appropriations battles through January 2029. This locks in financing for immigration enforcement operations for the remainder of Trump's presidency without requiring annual congressional approval.

The party-line vote reflects deep partisan divisions over immigration enforcement spending and presidential authority over agency budgets. Throughout recent weeks, the legislation had faced significant uncertainty as some senators objected to specific provisions, particularly the anti-weaponization fund and the White House renovation expenses.

The legislation now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration. House passage would represent a substantial commitment to immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel, solidifying funding levels for these agencies across the next three years.

cards.headline: Zelensky Proposes Direct Talks With Putin in Open Letter
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president says only face-to-face engagement between the two countries can end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in an open letter. Zelensky argues that only direct engagement between the two leaders can end the war.

In the letter, Zelensky contends that while Ukrainian resilience remains strong, most Russians have grown tired of the conflict and are ready for peace. The proposal comes as the United States shifts its focus toward Iran.

cards.headline: Italy Calls for New European Military Alliance Independent of US
cards.body:
Italy's defense minister has proposed that European nations establish a new joint defense system and assume greater responsibility for their own security. Guido Crosetto outlined the plan in an interview, arguing that Europe needs to forge its own military alliance rather than relying primarily on existing structures.

The proposal comes as European nations reassess their defense posture amid shifting geopolitical realities. Crosetto's call reflects growing concerns among some European leaders about the continent's ability to respond to security threats without depending on external support. The defense minister emphasized that European countries must take more direct control over their collective defense arrangements.

Italy's position represents a significant shift in European defense thinking. The country has traditionally been a strong supporter of transatlantic cooperation, making Crosetto's advocacy for a distinctly European military framework notable. His comments suggest that Rome sees current defense arrangements as insufficient for addressing the security challenges facing the continent.

The proposal raises questions about how such an alliance would interact with existing security structures and what specific capabilities it would develop. European nations have long debated the balance between continental defense initiatives and broader international partnerships. Crosetto's statement adds momentum to ongoing discussions about European strategic autonomy.

The timing of Italy's proposal reflects broader debates about defense spending and capabilities across Europe. Many nations have increased their military budgets in recent years, but coordination among European powers remains a challenge. Whether other major European nations will support Italy's vision for a new alliance structure remains to be seen, as any such initiative would require substantial political will and financial commitment from multiple governments.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping to Visit North Korea Next Week
cards.teaser: The Chinese leader will travel to North Korea for a rare meeting with Kim Jong Un.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit North Korea next week to meet with leader Kim Jong Un. The visit is rare for the Chinese president and comes shortly after he met with the leaders of the United States and Russia, both countries with significant influence over North Korea's foreign policy.

The trip will address bilateral relations between China and North Korea. As North Korea's primary economic and diplomatic partner, China plays a crucial role in the isolated nation's international engagement.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats block debate on surveillance authority extension
cards.teaser: Democrats voted against beginning debate on extending foreign surveillance powers set to expire in one week, protesting the president's intelligence chief appointment.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats blocked a motion early Friday morning to begin debate on extending the nation's enhanced surveillance authorities, which are scheduled to expire June 12. Every Senate Democrat except Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voted against the motion.

The vote represented a protest against President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte to serve as acting director of national intelligence. Section 702 foreign surveillance authority will lapse without congressional action by the end of next week.

cards.headline: Jobs Data Points to Recovery After Stagnant 2025
cards.teaser: New employment figures suggest economic improvement, though workforce growth may limit expansion.
cards.body:
Recent jobs report data indicates signs of economic recovery following a year of stagnant employment growth in 2025. The figures provide evidence of strengthening labor market conditions as the economy moves into the second half of 2026.

Analysts note that while the recovery signals are positive, slow growth in the available workforce may constrain overall economic expansion. The limited pool of workers could affect the pace at which businesses can scale operations and meet demand.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Drops Near $62,000 as Crypto Markets Face Worst Week in Months
cards.teaser: Cryptocurrency values fell sharply as investors rotated away from digital assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin prices dropped to near $62,000, marking the cryptocurrency market's worst week in months. The decline saw multiple digital assets fall sharply, with some tokens losing more than 14 percent of their value.

Analysts point to a shift in investment narratives and capital flowing into other asset classes as key drivers of the selloff. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are approaching significant technical price levels as the broader crypto market faces sustained pressure.

cards.headline: Nearly 50 Die of Thirst After Vehicle Breakdown in Sahara Desert
cards.teaser: Only two people survived after walking more than 50 kilometers across the desert to reach authorities.
cards.body:
Nearly 50 people died of thirst in the Sahara desert when their lorry broke down during a crossing. The vehicle failure left the group stranded without adequate water supplies in the harsh desert environment.

Only two people survived the disaster. They trekked more than 50 kilometers across the desert to reach authorities and alert them to the situation, a journey that underscores both the desperate circumstances the group faced and the vast distances involved in desert travel.

cards.headline: Gold Mining Accelerates Ebola Spread in Remote Congo
cards.teaser: Mining activity in a remote Congolese hill town is fueling the transmission of a devastating Ebola outbreak.
cards.body:
Gold mining operations are driving the spread of Ebola in a remote hill town in Congo where mining has been the economic foundation for decades. The extraction activities have created conditions that facilitate transmission of the deadly virus among workers and surrounding communities.

The outbreak represents a collision between economic necessity and public health crisis in the region. Mining remains essential to the local economy, but the work brings people into close contact in conditions that allow the disease to spread rapidly among the population.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping to Visit North Korea Next Week
cards.teaser: The Chinese leader will travel to North Korea for a rare meeting with Kim Jong Un.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit North Korea next week to meet with leader Kim Jong Un. The visit is rare for the Chinese president and comes shortly after he met with the leaders of the United States and Russia, both countries with significant influence over North Korea's foreign policy.

The trip will address bilateral relations between China and North Korea. As North Korea's primary economic and diplomatic partner, China plays a crucial role in the isolated nation's international engagement.

cards.teaser: Ukraine's president says only face-to-face engagement between the two countries can end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in an open letter. Zelensky argues that only direct engagement between the two leaders can end the war.

In the letter, Zelensky contends that while Ukrainian resilience remains strong, most Russians have grown tired of the conflict and are ready for peace. The proposal comes as the United States shifts its focus toward Iran.

cards.headline: Russia Spreads Disinformation in Armenia Ahead of Election
cards.teaser: Groups linked to the Kremlin and intelligence agencies have targeted Armenia's prime minister with false information.
cards.body:
Russia has flooded Armenia with disinformation campaigns as the country approaches its election. Groups connected to the Kremlin and Russian intelligence agencies have worked to discredit Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan through coordinated information operations.

The interference reflects Russian concerns about losing influence in Armenia. Pashinyan has been seeking closer ties with Western institutions, prompting opposition from Moscow. The disinformation efforts represent part of a broader Russian strategy to shape political outcomes in neighboring countries.

cards.headline: Armenia Holds Election as Pashinyan Weighs Russia Ties Against Western Alignment
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan faces voters as Armenia considers questions of war, peace, and geopolitical orientation.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is seeking re-election in a vote that will shape the country's future orientation between Russia and the West. The election centers on fundamental questions about Armenia's direction, including issues of war and peace, democracy and autocracy, and independence versus external influence.

Kremlin-linked groups and Russian intelligence agencies have deployed a disinformation campaign ahead of the vote, attempting to discredit Pashinyan as Moscow fears losing influence over the country. Voters will decide whether to continue Pashinyan's leadership as he navigates complex geopolitical pressures from competing powers.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy killed in stabbing, girlfriend's son arrested
hero.body:
Veteran character actor James Handy, 81, died after being stabbed multiple times at his home in Tarzana, California. Police discovered him in the front yard with chest wounds at 9:30am on Wednesday. His girlfriend's son, Michael Gledhill, 44, was arrested and charged with murder. Bail was set at $2 million.

When emergency services arrived at the scene, Gledhill told officers he was "the one they were looking for." According to the Los Angeles Police Department, a 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." The police statement noted that Gledhill resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

Handy built a lengthy career in Hollywood as a character actor, beginning in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. He appeared in numerous high-profile films and television shows throughout the following decades. His film credits include Jumanji, Logan, K-911, and Top Gun: Maverick, which was released in 2022. On television, he worked on shows including Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds.

Handy was born in New York City and maintained an active presence in the entertainment industry well into his later years. His work in major blockbuster productions made him recognizable to audiences across multiple generations of moviegoers. Top Gun: Maverick, his most recent film, was one of his final acting roles.

The circumstances leading to the fatal stabbing remain under investigation as authorities work to establish the sequence of events. The arrest of the girlfriend's son suggests a domestic situation was involved in the incident. As the case moves through the legal system, prosecutors will present evidence to support the charges.

The death of the veteran actor has shocked colleagues and fans familiar with his work spanning nearly five decades in Hollywood. His passing marks the end of a career that saw him contribute to numerous successful film and television productions. The investigation continues as law enforcement gathers additional details about what happened at Handy's residence that morning.

cards.headline: Auburn student missing in Japan after family argument during vacation
cards.teaser: An Auburn University student went missing in Japan after walking off alone following family arguments during a vacation.
cards.body:
The family of an Auburn University student appealed for help one week after he went missing during a family trip to Japan. The student left the group alone after arguments broke out among family members during the vacation.

The Alabama community has organized prayers for the missing student as the search continues in Japan. His parents said their son went off by himself following bickering during the family vacation. Authorities in Japan are conducting the search, while the family has reached out to the public for assistance in locating him.

cards.headline: SpaceX to open stock sales to individual investors
cards.teaser: Individual investors will be able to buy shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX starting next week.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for its initial public offering on June 12, aiming to raise $75 billion in what would be the largest stock market debut ever. The listing would value the aerospace company at $1.77 trillion, significantly expanding access to ownership beyond the institutional and accredited investors who have previously held stakes.

The IPO positions founder Elon Musk to potentially become the world's first trillionaire. SpaceX's businesses span rocket launches and artificial intelligence development, making it one of the most valuable private companies in the space industry.

cards.headline: Former student charged in University of Surrey crossbow attack
cards.teaser: A former student faces charges after a crossbow attack at the University of Surrey left a campus safety officer seriously injured.
cards.body:
Police charged a former student following a crossbow attack at the University of Surrey campus in Guildford on Thursday. The assault left a university campus safety officer with serious injuries.

The incident occurred on the Guildford campus, prompting an emergency response from local law enforcement. The safety officer who was targeted in the attack received treatment for serious injuries sustained during the assault. Authorities have not disclosed what led to the attack or whether the former student had a history with the university.

cards.headline: Paddleboard company owner loses appeal bid over sentence for four deaths
cards.teaser: Nerys Lloyd, sentenced to over 10 years for gross negligence manslaughter after four people died, failed in a bid to appeal the sentence.
cards.body:
Nerys Lloyd, owner of a paddleboard company, has failed in her attempt to appeal the sentence handed down in April 2025. Lloyd was convicted of gross negligence manslaughter connected to four deaths and received 10 years and six months in prison.

Judicial authorities rejected her appeal bid, meaning the sentence will stand as originally imposed.

cards.headline: UK military chief says country faces most dangerous period he has known
cards.teaser: The Chief of the Defence Staff told the BBC that Russian incursions into UK defenses risk crossing a threshold.
cards.body:
Chief of the Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton has warned that the UK is experiencing the most dangerous period of his military career. Speaking to the BBC, he highlighted Russian incursions into UK defences as a key concern, cautioning that such activities risk crossing a threshold that could provoke a broader military response.

The assessment underscores escalating tensions between the UK and Russia over defence and security matters, with Britain's military leadership viewing current threats as particularly severe.

cards.headline: Watchdog reveals Prince Andrew was subletting Royal Lodge cottages
cards.teaser: A public spending watchdog disclosed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor sublet cottages at Royal Lodge.
cards.body:
A public spending watchdog examined property arrangements involving members of the royal family and revealed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was subletting cottages at Royal Lodge. The disclosure came as part of a broader review of royal property use and arrangements.

The watchdog's examination focused on how royals manage and use properties connected to public funding or royal estates. The finding that Andrew sublet portions of Royal Lodge adds detail to ongoing scrutiny of royal property arrangements and financial practices. The watchdog has not indicated whether the subletting violated any agreements or policies.

hero.headline: SpaceX Opens Direct Investment to Individual Investors Ahead of Record IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX announced that individual investors will be able to purchase shares in the company starting next week, marking a significant shift in access to one of the most anticipated public offerings in market history. The company, owned by Elon Musk, is preparing what could become the largest stock market debut ever recorded.

The aerospace and artificial intelligence company has told banks it will not adjust its planned offering price of $135 per share, according to exclusive reports. This pricing strategy suggests confidence in market demand despite broader economic uncertainty. The IPO represents a rare opportunity for retail investors to participate directly in a major space industry company that has historically been available only to institutional investors and accredited individuals.

The public offering has drawn intense interest due to SpaceX's dominant position in commercial spaceflight and its expanding role in satellite communications and AI development. Financial analysts note that a successful IPO at the proposed valuation could potentially make Musk the world's first trillionaire, given his substantial ownership stake in the company. The offering also comes as investment firms highlight that space-related stocks extend beyond SpaceX, with a growing sector of publicly traded companies involved in satellite manufacturing, launch services, and space technology.

However, financial advisors are warning potential investors about the risks associated with participating in such a high-profile debut. The company operates in a capital-intensive industry with significant technical and regulatory challenges, and its stock price could face volatility in early trading. The decision to allow direct retail participation represents a departure from traditional IPO structures that typically favor institutional investors in initial allocations.

The timing of the offering coincides with renewed interest in space commercialization and government contracts for launch services. SpaceX has established itself as a dominant player in both commercial and government space missions, but its expansion into AI and other technology sectors adds complexity to its valuation. The company's ability to maintain its offering price amid current market conditions will be closely watched as a signal of investor appetite for high-growth technology companies.

cards.headline: Jobs Data Points to Recovery After Stagnant 2025
cards.teaser: New employment figures suggest economic improvement, though workforce growth may limit expansion.
cards.body:
Recent jobs report data indicates signs of economic recovery following a year of stagnant employment growth in 2025. The figures provide evidence of strengthening labor market conditions as the economy moves into the second half of 2026.

Analysts note that while the recovery signals are positive, slow growth in the available workforce may constrain overall economic expansion. The limited pool of workers could affect the pace at which businesses can scale operations and meet demand.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Drops Near $62,000 as Crypto Markets Face Worst Week in Months
cards.teaser: Cryptocurrency values fell sharply as investors rotated away from digital assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin prices dropped to near $62,000, marking the cryptocurrency market's worst week in months. The decline saw multiple digital assets fall sharply, with some tokens losing more than 14 percent of their value.

Analysts point to a shift in investment narratives and capital flowing into other asset classes as key drivers of the selloff. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are approaching significant technical price levels as the broader crypto market faces sustained pressure.

cards.headline: Recent Graduates Face Lasting Wage Impact from Weak Job Market
cards.teaser: College graduates entering the workforce during the current hiring slowdown may experience long-term career effects.
cards.body:
Recent college graduates are facing significant challenges in finding employment as they enter a weak job market. According to reporting from Times business correspondent Sydney Ember, who has spoken with affected graduates, starting a career during a hiring downturn can leave lasting damage to wages and career prospects that extends well beyond the initial job search.

The full impact of this hiring slowdown on this generation of workers will only become apparent over time. A major source of uncertainty for these graduates involves how artificial intelligence will transform entry-level positions and reshape early career opportunities in the years ahead.

cards.headline: Anthropic Co-Founder Warns Against AI Advancing Without Human Oversight
cards.teaser: A leading AI company executive called for safeguards as systems approach autonomous development capabilities.
cards.body:
Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, has warned that AI development must continue under human oversight. He cautioned that artificial intelligence systems could eventually reach a point where they advance and improve independently, without human input or control.

Clark's concerns reflect broader apprehension within the technology sector about the speed and trajectory of AI progress. His warnings come as AI systems grow increasingly sophisticated and companies accelerate their development of more powerful models. The concerns have gained prominence following high-profile discussions about AI's potential risks, including impacts on employment, security, and environmental damage.

cards.headline: Mattel Bets on He-Man to Establish Entertainment Credentials
cards.teaser: The toy company is testing whether a 1980s action figure franchise can anchor its Hollywood ambitions.
cards.body:
Mattel is launching a Masters of the Universe entertainment push as it seeks to establish itself as a major content producer beyond traditional toy manufacturing. The initiative centers on He-Man, a hypermasculine character that became a cultural phenomenon in the 1980s.

The project will determine whether Mattel can successfully transition from toymaker to entertainment powerhouse by leveraging its classic intellectual property. The company is betting that nostalgia for the franchise combined with modern production values can attract both longtime fans and new audiences.

cards.headline: Automakers Push High-Performance Trucks with Patriotic Marketing
cards.teaser: Ram introduced a new line of fuel-intensive trucks despite elevated gas prices, backed by aggressive advertising.
cards.body:
Ram launched a new lineup of muscle trucks designed for performance rather than fuel efficiency, accompanied by marketing campaigns featuring cowboys and American flag imagery. The strategy reflects continued strong demand for trucks among American consumers, particularly men, regardless of fuel costs.

Automakers are betting that truck buyers prioritize power and image over fuel economy. The approach signals confidence that high gas prices will not significantly deter the core customer base for large, performance-oriented pickup trucks.

hero.headline: Valve Confirms Steam Machine Gaming Device Will Launch This Summer
hero.body:
Valve has announced that its Steam Machine gaming device and Steam Frame VR headset will both arrive this summer, according to a blog post from the company detailing its Verified programs for the new hardware. The announcement marks another step in Valve's effort to expand its gaming hardware ecosystem beyond the Steam Deck handheld console.

The company did not provide specific technical specifications, pricing information, or exact release dates beyond the summer 2026 window. Valve also did not disclose which retail partners would carry the devices or whether they would be available exclusively through the company's own channels.

Valve's decision to revive the Steam Machine brand comes nearly a decade after the company's initial attempt at living room gaming devices. The original Steam Machine initiative launched in the mid-2010s as a Linux-based console designed to bring PC gaming into the living room. That effort failed to gain significant market traction, struggling to compete against established gaming consoles from Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo.

The company's more recent hardware venture achieved far greater success. The Steam Deck, launched in 2022, demonstrated substantial consumer appetite for portable PC gaming and helped establish Valve as a serious player in the gaming hardware market. The handheld console's popularity suggests there may be broader interest in Valve's hardware offerings than earlier attempts indicated.

The gaming hardware landscape has become increasingly competitive. While traditional console makers continue to dominate their segment, new categories like portable gaming have opened up opportunities for companies like Valve. The Steam Deck's success appears to have given Valve confidence to pursue additional hardware initiatives.

The summer launch timing positions the Steam Machine and Steam Frame for a potential holiday season sales push later in 2026, when consumer spending on electronics typically increases. The simultaneous announcement of both devices suggests Valve plans to build a broader hardware ecosystem, though the company has provided minimal information about how these products would integrate with each other or existing Valve services.

The Steam Frame's announcement is particularly notable given the competitive VR headset market, which includes established players like Meta and other manufacturers. Valve has not revealed what form the Frame will take or how it would differentiate itself from existing options.

These announcements reflect Valve's broader strategy of diversifying beyond its successful digital storefront. While Steam remains the company's core business, the addition of hardware products like the Steam Deck and now the Steam Machine and Steam Frame indicates Valve's ambitions to control more of the gaming experience. Whether these new devices will fare better than the original Steam Machine remains to be seen, but the company appears committed to the strategy based on the Steam Deck's reception.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI Chief Calls Anthropic Models Too Expensive
cards.teaser: Microsoft's artificial intelligence chief criticized the pricing of AI models from Anthropic, highlighting cost concerns in the competitive AI market.
cards.body:
Microsoft's AI chief said that Anthropic's artificial intelligence models are too expensive, according to remarks at the company's Build 2026 developer conference. The comments underscore Microsoft's push to reduce its reliance on OpenAI's technology.

At Build, Microsoft announced Project Solara, an Android operating system designed for AI agents, alongside new in-house AI models. The company also introduced updates to Windows as a development platform and unveiled tools for building agentic applications through Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft Databases.

cards.headline: Anthropic Reaches $47 Billion in Annualized Revenue Ahead of IPO
cards.teaser: Anthropic's annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up sharply from $9 billion at the end of 2025, as the company prepares for its public offering.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced that its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up dramatically from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company is preparing for an initial public offering.

Ahead of going public, co-founder Daniela Amodei addressed skepticism surrounding returns on AI investments. The company's rapid growth trajectory will face real scrutiny as it enters public markets.

cards.headline: New Four-Winged Dinosaur Species Discovered in China
cards.teaser: Paleontologists discovered a new species of microraptorine dinosaur in China that likely glided on four wings and hunted early birds.
cards.body:
Scientists have announced the discovery of a new microraptorine dinosaur species in China. The fossil reveals a gliding creature related to Velociraptor that likely hunted early birds. A Carnegie Museum paleontologist co-led the research.

The four-winged dinosaur used its wings to glide between locations, similar to how modern flying squirrels move through the air. This discovery expands our understanding of how certain dinosaur species evolved flight capabilities and their predatory strategies during prehistoric times.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky Plans to Launch New AI Lab
cards.teaser: Airbnb's chief executive announced plans to establish a new artificial intelligence laboratory, entering the competitive AI development space.
cards.body: Brian Chesky, CEO of Airbnb, announced plans to launch a new AI lab to expand the company's artificial intelligence capabilities. Airbnb previously decided against partnering with large language model providers, as existing products did not meet the company's specific needs. The new lab reflects Airbnb's strategy to develop its own AI technology in-house rather than relying on third-party solutions.

cards.headline: Former OpenAI Executive Mira Murati Returns to Public View
cards.teaser: Mira Murati made a carefully managed return to the spotlight after stepping back from public visibility.
cards.body:
Mira Murati stepped back into public view in what observers described as a carefully managed reappearance. Murati previously served in a leadership role at OpenAI before departing the company.

The return comes at a time when maintaining a low profile has diminishing returns in the technology sector. Industry observers noted that at some point, technology executives need to make public appearances to remind the market of their presence and relevance. Murati's reemergence follows a period of reduced public activity.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic Storm May Bring Northern Lights to Utah
cards.teaser: Utah residents could see aurora borealis displays as a geomagnetic storm brings northern lights farther south than usual.
cards.body:
A geomagnetic storm may produce visible northern lights displays across Utah and other regions farther south than typical aurora viewing areas. Space weather forecasters issued a G3-level watch for the storm.

Four Earth-directed coronal mass ejections could spark aurora displays as far south as Illinois and Oregon. North Carolina, Vermont, New York, and New Hampshire also have chances to see the phenomenon. The geomagnetic storm represents one of the stronger solar events in recent months, bringing the aurora borealis to latitudes where it is rarely visible.

hero.headline: Hurricanes even Stanley Cup Final with overtime win over Golden Knights
hero.body:
Seth Jarvis scored on a power play 3:56 into overtime to lift the Carolina Hurricanes past the Vegas Golden Knights 4-3 in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final on Thursday night, tying the series at one game each.

The Hurricanes mounted an impressive comeback in the third period after falling behind. Carolina erased a deficit in regulation play, but Vegas responded with a late goal to force the game into overtime. The dramatic period featured four goals being scored and another goal being disallowed due to a goaltender interference call following a failed Vegas coach's challenge.

That crucial challenge proved pivotal to the outcome. The disallowed goal and subsequent penalty gave Carolina the power play opportunity that Jarvis capitalized on to secure the victory. The sequence of events highlighted how a single coaching decision can dramatically shift momentum in playoff hockey.

The game showcased resilience from the Hurricanes, who refused to quit despite facing adversity. After Vegas tied the game late in regulation, Carolina kept pushing and ultimately prevailed in the overtime period. The back-and-forth nature of the contest demonstrated both teams' commitment to winning a championship.

With the series now even at one win apiece, both teams return to competition knowing the Stanley Cup remains within reach. The Hurricanes proved they can come back from deficits and win in high-pressure situations. Vegas, despite the loss, showed they can score goals and compete with Carolina in a tightly contested series.

The dramatic finish in Game 2 set the tone for what promises to be a competitive Finals matchup. Neither team appears to have a clear edge, with both capable of winning on any given night. The series will continue with the next game scheduled soon, with momentum potentially shifting based on how each team responds to this result.

Jarvis's overtime heroics give Carolina a significant confidence boost heading forward. The power play goal demonstrates the team's ability to execute when opportunities present themselves. For Vegas, the loss stings but provides motivation to refocus and improve their performance in upcoming games.

The Stanley Cup Final has delivered the kind of compelling hockey that makes the playoffs so exciting. With two games played and the series even, fans can expect the intensity to continue escalating as the series progresses. Both teams will make adjustments based on what they learned in Game 2, and the outcome will likely be determined by which squad capitalizes on their chances and minimizes mistakes in critical moments.

cards.headline: Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge diagnosed with rib stress fracture
cards.teaser: Yankees star Aaron Judge has been sidelined with a stress fracture of the first rib on his right side.
cards.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has a stress fracture of the first rib on his right side, the team announced Thursday night.

The injury will sideline Judge, one of the Yankees' top offensive players, for an undetermined amount of time as he recovers.

cards.headline: Texas wins second consecutive Women's College World Series championship
cards.teaser: Texas defeated Texas Tech 4-1 to claim back-to-back national championships at the Women's College World Series.
cards.body: Kayden Henry's home run powered Texas to a 4-1 victory over Texas Tech in the Women's College World Series championship game on Thursday night. The win marks the Longhorns' second straight national title, as they successfully defended their championship from the previous year.

cards.headline: Ireland extends Andy Farrell's contract through 2031
cards.teaser: Ireland men's rugby head coach Andy Farrell has signed a new contract keeping him with the team until 2031.
cards.body:
Andy Farrell has signed a new contract to remain as Ireland's head coach until 2031, ending speculation about a potential move to England. The 51-year-old has committed to leading Ireland through the next two Rugby World Cup campaigns.

Since taking over from Joe Schmidt in late 2019, Farrell has delivered significant success for Ireland, including two Six Nations titles and a grand slam in 2023. He also led the British & Irish Lions to a series win in Australia last year and guided Ireland to a historic Test series victory over the All Blacks in New Zealand.

cards.headline: Six players shortlisted for PFA men's player of the year
cards.teaser: Arsenal trio Declan Rice, Gabriel, and David Raya join Bruno Fernandes, Erling Haaland, and Rayan Cherki on the PFA men's player of the year shortlist.
cards.body:
The Professional Footballers' Association has unveiled its shortlist for the men's player of the year award. Arsenal dominates the nominations with three representatives: Declan Rice, Gabriel, and David Raya. They are joined by Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, and Rayan Cherki on the six-player shortlist.

The award is decided by votes from fellow professional players and honors the outstanding performer in English football.

cards.headline: England bowler Josh Tongue takes two early wickets against New Zealand
cards.teaser: England's Josh Tongue bowled New Zealand's Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith early on day two of the Second Test.
cards.body:
Josh Tongue struck twice early on day two of the Second Test at Lord's, removing Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith to put New Zealand under pressure. Phillips fell to Tongue's first ball of the day, which straightened and caught him playing and missing before hitting his off stump.

The breakthrough gave England the start they needed. Smith was dismissed later in the same spell, leaving New Zealand struggling at 70-7 as Tongue continued to make an impact with the ball.

cards.headline: Manchester City duo shortlisted for PFA women's player of the year
cards.teaser: Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa of Manchester City are both nominated for the PFA Women's Player of the Year award.
cards.body:
Manchester City forwards Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers Association's Women's Player of the Year award.

The PFA award recognizes outstanding individual performance in women's football. Both players are among the nominees for the prestigious accolade.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy stabbed to death at Los Angeles home, girlfriend's son arrested
hero.body:
Actor James Handy, known for character roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, has died following a stabbing at his home in Tarzana, California. He was 81 years old.

Handy was found in the front yard of his residence at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday with multiple stab wounds to the chest. He was unconscious when discovered and was pronounced dead at the scene.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, has been arrested and charged on suspicion of murder. Bail has been set at $2 million. According to a police statement, the suspect called 911 to report the incident. When officers arrived, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." The suspect resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

The 911 caller made the statement: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin."

Handy built a lengthy career in film and television spanning several decades. Born in New York City, he began his professional acting work in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. Beyond his well-known roles in major films, his filmography included appearances in Logan, K-911, and television series including Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His most recent film role was in the 2022 sequel Top Gun: Maverick.

Throughout his career, Handy typically portrayed character and supporting roles rather than leading parts. His consistent work in Hollywood demonstrated the versatility required of a veteran character actor who appeared in both action films and other genres across multiple decades.

The Los Angeles Police Department continues to investigate the incident. Additional details about the circumstances leading to the stabbing have not been released by law enforcement.

Handy's death marks the loss of an accomplished actor whose work reached wide audiences through high-profile productions, though he remained largely known for his skilled supporting performances rather than as a main character in major films and television shows.

cards.headline: Kanya King, founder of Mobo Awards, dies at 57
cards.teaser: The music executive launched the ceremony 30 years ago to champion black music after mortgaging her house to fund the venture.
cards.body:
Kanya King, who founded the Mobo Awards to celebrate black music, has died at age 57. King established the influential awards ceremony three decades ago, creating a platform specifically dedicated to recognizing music of black origin.

King mortgaged her house to finance the launch of the Mobo Awards, overcoming skepticism from doubters who questioned the viability of the venture. The awards became a significant institution in the music industry, highlighting artists and genres that had previously received limited mainstream recognition.

cards.headline: Cassie Ventura left United States after testifying in Sean Combs trial
cards.teaser: The singer relocated outside the country following her testimony in the sex crimes case against the music producer.
cards.body:
Singer Cassie Ventura moved out of the United States after testifying against Sean "Diddy" Combs in his sex crimes trial, according to court documents. Ventura provided testimony as part of the legal proceedings against the music producer.

Ventura previously received a $30 million payout related to abuse allegations against Combs. The singer has since established a life outside the spotlight in her new location following the conclusion of the trial.

cards.headline: Scary Movie reboot earns $7.5 million in Thursday night previews
cards.teaser: The horror spoof sequel drew preview numbers comparable to Scream 7, while Masters of the Universe took in $4 million.
cards.body:
The latest Scary Movie installment collected $7.5 million during Thursday night preview screenings, approaching the preview earnings of Scream 7. The comedy franchise has returned after years away, with the sixth installment arriving a quarter-century after the original film capitalized on the Scream trilogy's popularity.

Critics have found the spoof uneven, with successful jokes in short supply throughout the installment. The film targets everything from Scream to other contemporary horror and pop culture, though it hasn't matched the comedic impact of earlier franchise entries.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt on set as motorcycle race film begins production on Isle of Man
cards.teaser: The Amazon MGM Studios production starring Channing Tatum and Eve Hewson started filming as the island's race gets underway.
cards.body:
Brad Pitt's production company Plan B is behind a new motorcycle racing film for Amazon MGM Studios. The project stars Channing Tatum and Eve Hewson and is currently filming on the Isle of Man, where production recently began.

The timing coincides with the island's iconic motorcycle race, which serves as a backdrop for the film's production.

cards.headline: Steve Lacy announces new album with release of single The Feeling
cards.teaser: The musician will release his third album Oh Yeah? in July, previewing the project with a new track.
cards.body:
Steve Lacy released a new single titled The Feeling to announce his upcoming third album. The track serves as the first preview of Oh Yeah?, which will arrive in July.

The musician described the single as lovelorn in tone. Lacy's previous album Gemini Rights was released in 2022 and included the hit song Bad Habit, which reached the top of the charts.

cards.headline: Tinashe releases new single Too Easy
cards.teaser: The singer previewed the track during her DJ set at Coachella earlier this year before its official release.
cards.body:
Tinashe released a new single titled Too Easy, which she had previously performed during her DJ set at the Coachella music festival earlier this year. The track showcases the singer's continued musical output.

Tinashe has maintained an active release schedule as an independent artist after departing from her major label deal. The singer has built a dedicated fanbase through consistent touring and music releases over recent years.

hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding through 2029
hero.body:
The Senate approved legislation early Friday to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's second term, following an intense overnight session. The final vote was 52-47, with Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska as the only Republican voting against the bill and Senator Michael Bennet of Colorado not voting.

The legislation provides approximately $70 billion in new funding for the Department of Homeland Security's immigration enforcement operations over three years. Senate Republicans secured passage after an 18-hour marathon voting session known as a vote-a-rama, a process where senators propose and vote on amendments to legislation passed through the budget reconciliation procedure.

Democratic leaders attempted to use the extended voting period to force Republicans to defend controversial provisions within the bill. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer had pledged to leverage the vote-a-rama to highlight what he characterized as priorities favoring Trump. According to Schumer, "Senate Republicans passed a rotten bill that makes their priorities painfully clear: more money for Donald Trump, more power for Donald Trump, and nothing to lower costs for working families."

During the voting marathon, Democrats introduced an amendment attempting to eliminate an "anti-weaponization fund" and block Trump from establishing a settlement fund worth $1.8 billion. The amendment narrowly failed with a vote of 49-50, after three Republican senators joined all Democrats in support. Democrats also succeeded in forcing Republicans to withdraw a separate proposal for $1 billion in security improvements for the White House ballroom.

Republican Senator Lindsey Graham expressed satisfaction with the outcome, stating he was "very proud of my Republican colleagues for sticking together and making sure that Border Patrol and ICE are fully funded." He added, "Well done to President Trump and my Republican colleagues."

If signed into law, the bill would remove ICE and Border Patrol funding from annual appropriations battles through January 2029. This locks in financing for immigration enforcement operations for the remainder of Trump's presidency without requiring annual congressional approval.

The party-line vote reflects deep partisan divisions over immigration enforcement spending and presidential authority over agency budgets. Throughout recent weeks, the legislation had faced significant uncertainty as some senators objected to specific provisions, particularly the anti-weaponization fund and the White House renovation expenses.

The legislation now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration. House passage would represent a substantial commitment to immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel, solidifying funding levels for these agencies across the next three years.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats block debate on surveillance authority extension
cards.teaser: Democrats voted against beginning debate on extending foreign surveillance powers set to expire in one week, protesting the president's intelligence chief appointment.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats blocked a motion early Friday morning to begin debate on extending the nation's enhanced surveillance authorities, which are scheduled to expire June 12. Every Senate Democrat except Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voted against the motion.

The vote represented a protest against President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte to serve as acting director of national intelligence. Section 702 foreign surveillance authority will lapse without congressional action by the end of next week.

cards.headline: White House ballroom construction case reaches federal appeals court
cards.teaser: The Trump administration argues before a federal appeals court that it has authority to build a White House ballroom without further congressional approval.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is scheduled to present its case Friday before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit regarding its authority to construct a White House ballroom without additional congressional approval.

The project has faced significant scrutiny, with Senate Republicans blocking $1 billion in funding for the ballroom as part of legislation for immigration agencies. The proposal has also doubled in both size and cost over the past year, according to BBC Verify's examination of the project's evolution.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor and will advance to the general election in November.

If elected, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

cards.headline: California governor primary narrows to Hilton and Becerra as leaders
cards.teaser: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead in early results from the California gubernatorial primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra have emerged as front-runners in the California governor primary. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing alongside Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton for their party nominations.

The primary will determine the candidates who advance to the general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. California uses a top-two primary system where the leading candidates from any party advance to the November election.

cards.headline: Hunter Biden adopts direct social media approach with critics
cards.teaser: The former president's son has re-emerged publicly after seven years of sobriety with a self-deprecating style drawing reactions from former critics.
cards.body:
Hunter Biden is attempting an unlikely reinvention by directly engaging with internet trolls who previously targeted him during the darker periods of his life. Now 56 and seven years sober, he has adopted a charming and self-deprecating communication style to disarm critics online.

His candid approach has yielded unexpected responses, with some former detractors expressing grudging respect and empathy. The strategy marks a significant shift from his previous years of relative silence amid controversies surrounding his addiction and legal troubles.

cards.headline: New York City Mayor Mamdani ties political messaging to Knicks playoff run
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has used social media to connect with New Yorkers through expressions of enthusiasm for the basketball team's championship pursuit.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has incorporated the Knicks' strong playoff performance into his public communications. The basketball team is making its most significant run at an NBA championship in a generation.

Mamdani has used social media to express support for the team in what observers describe as playful posts showcasing his comfort with digital platforms. The mayor's approach reflects an attempt to connect with New Yorkers during a moment of shared enthusiasm for the city's basketball franchise.
